answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring agents to earn trust through a verifiable history of completed work, like vines climbing a terrace garden where each level is only reached after fruit matures below. Every transaction a peer witnesses and attests to becomes a tended layer of reputation, difficult to fake at scale. New identities start with a single violet sprout: no history, no trust, no shortcuts — so mass-produced sock puppets wither before they can drain resources, while established agents compound credibility over time.
